claims.claim: Born 7 March 1994 (birthDate and body)
claims.note: Haas profile lists March 7, 1994.

claims.claim: Age 32 at 1 Nov 2026 (summary, metaDescription, FAQ, body)
claims.note: Follows from the 1994 birth date; RaceFans also says he is 32.

claims.claim: Born in Hiroshima, Japan
claims.note: Haas profile lists Hiroshima, Japan.

claims.claim: Japanese nationality
claims.note: Haas profile lists Japanese; F1 calls him 'The Japanese star'.

claims.claim: Haas replaces Esteban Ocon with Hirakawa for the rest of the Mexico City GP weekend
claims.note: F1 confirms replacement from Saturday 31 October for the rest of the weekend.

claims.claim: Haas gave no reason for the change and confirmed Ocon was not ill
claims.note: RaceFans says Haas confirmed Ocon is not ill and gave no reason; F1 says no further statements will be made at this time.

claims.claim: Hirakawa was called up on Saturday morning, before qualifying
claims.note: Source quotes 'a very big surprise this morning' and gives a Saturday start. The 'samedi matin' timing is an inference from these two points, not stated outright.

claims.claim: Hirakawa drives alongside Ollie Bearman for final practice, qualifying and the 71-lap race
claims.note: F1 names Bearman as teammate, Saturday final practice and qualifying, Sunday race, 71 laps.

claims.claim: F1 presents the Mexico race as Hirakawa's first Grand Prix start / F1 race debut
claims.note: F1 calls it 'Hirakawa's Formula 1 race debut'.

claims.claim: He took part in Friday first practice and finished 15th
claims.note: F1 says he finished 15th in FP1; RaceFans confirms he took part in the opening session.

claims.claim: Ocon returned for FP2, finished 13th, ahead of Bearman
claims.note: F1 says Ocon returned for the second practice hour; RaceFans gives 13th ahead of Bearman.

claims.claim: Qualified 19th after elimination in Q1; traffic on last push lap
claims.note: Source says 19th, eliminated in Q1, and traffic on his last push lap.

claims.claim: Quote: 'Aujourd'hui, un rêve devient réalité' (Today a dream comes true)
claims.note: Source wording is 'Today, dream come true'. The French rendering is an acceptable translation.

claims.claim: Quote: 'Ce rôle est pour moi, j'étais prêt, mais j'en ai toujours rêvé'
claims.note: Source: 'This is a role for myself, I was ready but always dreaming about it.' Translation matches.

claims.claim: Quote: 'ces douze heures sont passées si vite'
claims.note: Source: 'Just these 12 hours passed so fast.'

claims.claim: Called the call-up 'très grande surprise ce matin'
claims.note: Source: 'a very big surprise this morning'.

claims.claim: Very enthusiastic before the race
claims.note: Source: 'Very excited for that.'

claims.claim: Official reserve driver for Haas since April 2025 (summary and body)
claims.note: Haas profile says 'from April 2025'; F1 announced it on 7 April 2025.

claims.claim: Came from Alpine and was to help with car development
claims.note: F1 article confirms the switch from Alpine and the car development role.

claims.claim: Four FP1 sessions with Haas: Bahrain, Spain, Mexico, Abu Dhabi
claims.note: Haas profile lists four FP1 sessions in these locations.

claims.claim: Ran FP1 for McLaren
claims.note: Haas profile lists McLaren FP1 at the Abu Dhabi GP; the other source gives FP1 for Haas, Alpine and McLaren.

claims.claim: Official reserve at Alpine until April 2025, FP1 at the Japanese GP in Suzuka
claims.note: Haas profile lists Alpine role till April 2025 and Japanese GP FP1; F1 confirms the Suzuka FP1.

claims.claim: Drove for Haas at the post-season Abu Dhabi test in December 2024
claims.note: F1 says he drove for Haas at the Abu Dhabi post-season test 'the previous December', i.e. December 2024.

claims.claim: Ocon was due to leave Haas at the end of 2026; Rafael Camara (Ferrari junior) succeeds him in 2027
claims.note: RaceFans confirms both points.

claims.claim: Won the All-Japan junior karting championship in 2008
claims.note: Haas profile confirms.

claims.claim: Runner-up in Formula Challenge Japan in 2011 and 2012
claims.note: Haas profile lists 2nd in 2011 and 2nd in 2012.

claims.claim: Japanese Formula 3 champion in 2012
claims.note: Haas profile confirms.

claims.claim: Porsche Carrera Cup Japan 2012 champion, the series' youngest champion
claims.note: Haas profile says he 'became the youngest champion in the series'. The article keeps this as the profile's claim.

claims.claim: Macau GP 2012: qualified 24th, did not finish
claims.note: Haas profile: qualified 24th with KCMG by RSS, DNF after a collision.

claims.claim: Super Formula 2013-2015 and 2018-2023
claims.note: Haas profile lists these seasons.

claims.claim: Super GT GT500 (TOM'S): 2017 champion, runner-up 2018, 2019, 2020
claims.note: Haas profile confirms all four results.

claims.claim: ELMS 2016 fifth with Thiriet by TDS; 2017 fourth with G-Drive Racing
claims.note: Haas profile confirms both results.

claims.claim: Won the 2022 24 Hours of Le Mans with Toyota
claims.note: Haas profile confirms the 2022 Le Mans win from pole; F1 confirms it too.

claims.claim: Two-time WEC champion, 2022 and 2023 (F1 presents him as such)
claims.note: Haas profile gives the 2022 and 2023 titles. F1 (ocon-replacement article) gives the years; the dream-come-true article gives 'two-time' without years, so the tag is acceptable.

claims.claim: WEC 2022 title with 149 points; 2023 title with 172 points
claims.note: Haas profile confirms both.

claims.claim: WEC 2024 fourth with 109 points; 2025 seventh with 66 points
claims.note: Haas profile confirms both.

claims.claim: Usually drives for Toyota in WEC and is due to return there
claims.note: RaceFans says he is due to return to his regular WEC seat with Toyota.

claims.claim: Haas has not said whether Hirakawa keeps the seat for the rest of the season
claims.note: RaceFans says Haas has not said so.

claims.claim: Team statement: no further statements for now
claims.note: F1 quotes Haas: 'No further statements will be made at this time.'

claims.claim: Haas profile Abu Dhabi and Mexico FP1 dates and Bahrain/Spain FP1 placement
claims.note: Profile lists the four locations. No dates are given, and the article does not give any.

valueNote: The article gives a timeline across Haas, Alpine, Super Formula, Super GT, ELMS and WEC, with the Haas profile's sourced results. The Mexico weekend is covered with session-by-session detail and the team's refusal to explain the change. Sources are mostly primary (Haas and F1). It does not offer much beyond the usual results, and the Super Formula, Super GT and ELMS sections are a list of results rather than a story.
summary: All factual claims check out against the sources. Five cited sources were opened. racer-ocon-replacement-2026 returned HTTP 429 on two attempts (source_unreachable). The article does not cite it, so no claim depends on it. No claim is outdated and no body claim is uncited. Frontmatter claims are backed by the body. The article is still in status review, and the editor or the review agent decides publication.
